about: Known answers for the poll loop of a native client (README section 5.1.1: DK-03, MOB-21a). Each case gives the client's counters before the answer, what the relay answered (or that nothing came), the jitter draw u, and what the rules lead to: the outcome (P2), the pause before jitter and after it (P3, P5, P6), the counters after, what the loop does when it ends (P8) and what it reports (P7). A case with `replace` is rule P1 (the earliest a replacement poll may start). Both readers recompute every case from the rules, not from this file's other cases.

cases.what: a client that cancels a running poll and starts another waits until 250 ms have passed since it started the first (0 ms have)
a client that cancels a running poll and starts another waits until 250 ms have passed since it started the first (100 ms have)
a client that cancels a running poll and starts another waits until 250 ms have passed since it started the first (249 ms have)
a client that cancels a running poll and starts another waits until 250 ms have passed since it started the first (250 ms have)
a client that cancels a running poll and starts another waits until 250 ms have passed since it started the first (5000 ms have)
a 200 with an item is progress: no pause, every counter cleared
a 200 with reset:true and no items is progress too (the client adopts the cursor, section 5.1)
an empty 200 is idle: wait info.wait.pollGapMs (250 ms) before the next poll
the pause is the base plus up to 20 percent of it: u = 0.5 adds 10 percent
a relay whose gap is 0 asks for no pause
the longest gap the relay allows is 5000 ms
a poll this client replaced answers superseded: discarded, no pause, nothing started
a poll this client did not replace was replaced by another process of the same credential: reported
a refused hold is idle: the first pause is hold.retryAfter
the second refused hold in a row doubles the pause
the third reaches info.wait.fallbackS (5), not 8
and stays there
a refused hold with no retryAfter is read as 2
a retryAfter beyond the fallback is honoured, never shortened
a retryAfter of 0 is clamped to 1
a granted hold that ends empty is idle and clears the count of refused holds
a 200 whose body is not a JSON object is a failure: pause 1, the failure count rises
a 200 whose body is empty or not JSON is a failure: pause 1, the failure count rises
a 200 object without items is a failure: pause 1, the failure count rises
a 200 whose items is not an array is a failure: pause 1, the failure count rises
the gap rule's 429 (Retry-After 1) is flow control: pause 1, the 429 count rises, the failure count is cleared
the 2th 429 in a row (Retry-After 1) pauses 2 seconds
the 3th 429 in a row (Retry-After 1) pauses 4 seconds
the 4th 429 in a row (Retry-After 1) pauses 8 seconds
the 5th 429 in a row (Retry-After 1) pauses 16 seconds
the 6th 429 in a row (Retry-After 1) pauses 30 seconds
the 9th 429 in a row (Retry-After 1) pauses 30 seconds
the 31th 429 in a row (Retry-After 1) pauses 30 seconds
the fifth 429 in a row with rule in_flight is a defect to report
the fourth is not yet
five 429s of the gap rule are not that defect (they are the pause of P3 not being kept, which P4 says)
a sixth is reported no more (once)
a Retry-After longer than the backoff is honoured: 7 seconds on the first 429
and a backoff longer than the Retry-After wins: the fourth 429 in a row pauses 8 seconds though the relay said 7
a Retry-After of 600 is clamped to 120
and the jitter is added after the clamp: 120 with u = 0.9 is 141.6
a Retry-After of 0 is clamped to 1: a client never spins
no header: error.retryAfter is read
neither: 1 second for a 429
an HTTP-date is the seconds from the Date header of the answer: 10
an HTTP-date that has passed is 0, so 1
with no Date header the client's own clock stands in: 7 seconds
an unreadable Date header is as good as none: the client's own clock stands in (7 seconds), and the body's 4 is not read
a header that is text is no header: the body's 4 is read
a signed number is no header
a fraction is no header
seven digits are no header
spaces around the digits are trimmed
leading zeros are digits
error.retryAfter above 86400 is not read
error.retryAfter that is a boolean is not read
a rule the client does not know is treated as none
a bucket's 429 (no rule) is flow control too, and the pause is its Retry-After
a 429 from a proxy with an HTML body is flow control too
a 429 proves the relay answered: the failure count is cleared, the 429 count is not
no response: the first failure pauses 1
the second pauses 2
the third pauses 4 and the relay is reported unreachable
and the fourth reports it again (the report is a state, not an event: it holds until a success or a 429)
the sixth pauses 32
the seventh is capped at 60
and stays at 60
a 408 is a failure: pause 1, failure count 1
a 500 is a failure: pause 1, failure count 1
a 502 is a failure: pause 1, failure count 1
a 504 is a failure: pause 1, failure count 1
a 501 is a failure: pause 1, failure count 1
a 505 is a failure: pause 1, failure count 1
a 503 with Retry-After 30 pauses 30
a Retry-After of 600 on a 503 is 120
a 503 with no Retry-After pauses by the backoff alone
a 503's Retry-After 2 does not shorten the fourth failure's 8
a 301 is a failure and is not followed
a failure clears the 429 count
the jitter applies to failures too: a 4 second pause with u = 0.25 is 4.2
any success clears the failure count (and with it the report)
401 unauthorized: the credential is not accepted: refresh it once or enrol again; the loop does not retry
401 revoked: the device was revoked: forget the credential
426: end the loop and tell the user to update
400 invalid_request: a defect of the client or a relay that is off: end the loop and report the code
